analysis.investment_thesis: Carborundum Universal is a decent industrial franchise with modest brand recognition in abrasives and ceramics, but it earns subpar returns on equity and commands a wildly excessive 74x trailing P/E for what is fundamentally a low-margin, capital-intensive industrial business. The sharp net profit collapse in FY2025 (from INR 476 Cr to INR 299 Cr, a 37% drop) and near-zero free cash flow of INR 28 Cr in 2025 make the premium valuation impossible to justify.
key_strengths: Nearly debt-free balance sheet with D/E of only 0.08, providing financial resilience during downturns
Revenue has compounded at a steady 10.8% CAGR over 9 years with consistent operating cash flow (5/5 years positive)
Diversified product mix across abrasives, technical ceramics, and electrominerals gives some end-market breadth
key_risks: ROE of only 10.8% — well below my 15% threshold — indicating the business does not earn exceptional returns on shareholder capital
Net profit collapsed 37% in FY2025 (INR 476 Cr → INR 299 Cr) with other income swinging to -INR 23 Cr, revealing earnings quality concerns
FCF nearly evaporated to just INR 28 Cr in FY2025 despite INR 278 Cr in capex, signalling rising capital intensity without commensurate returns
red_flags: P/E of 74x is extreme for a business with 7.43% operating margins — this is a fair business at a terrible price
EV/EBITDA of 32x and forward P/E of 39x remain expensive even under optimistic recovery assumptions
Operating margin of 7.43% offers almost no buffer against cost inflation or demand weakness
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Carborundum Universal has built a respectable 70-year franchise in abrasives and industrial ceramics, but this is not the kind of business that earns the exceptional returns I require. ROE of 10.8% and operating margins of 7.43% are the hallmarks of a commoditised industrial supplier, not a business with durable pricing power. The FY2025 earnings collapse — net profit down 37%, other income turning sharply negative, FCF down to INR 28 Cr from INR 367 Cr — suggests the underlying earnings power is weaker than the prior year's numbers implied. Capex is accelerating (INR 278 Cr in 2025) even as returns deteriorate, a pattern I find troubling.

At 74x trailing P/E and 32x EV/EBITDA, the market is pricing this as if Carborundum were a high-quality compounder. It is not. I need a margin of safety, and at these prices I have the opposite — a significant margin of danger. A fair price for this business would be closer to 20-25x earnings, implying 65-70% downside to intrinsic value from current levels. I would not buy this at any price close to today's.
